method: The same evaluator sealed an unaided baseline before reading docs, catalog, code, or web.
Then read AGENTS.md, README.md, example briefs, contract, and CLI help; did not fetch or rebuild sources.
Used the four supplied examples, preserving eligible existing baselines. Compared top three alternatives plus baseline where available.
Used inspect, family, and resolve for every final exact face, and opened the seven final comparison PNGs plus four supplemental comparison PNGs.
Implementation changed during formative feedback. Early observations and the final stable recapture are distinguished. The evaluator edited only evaluation scripts/artifacts, not implementation.

suggestions.reason: A restrained interface family with recognizable letterforms and a useful range of weights; a plausible fit for dense operational labels.
suggestions.caveat: Inspect the actual 0/O/1/l glyphs at control size. Do not assume a slashed zero, tabular numerals, or exact Regular/Bold files without checking the chosen build.

briefs.judgment_basis: Subjective visual inspection by one agent; not a readability study.
briefs.decision: Keep IBM Plex Sans as the provisional UI baseline; no reviewed finalist earns an unconditional pass for the strict 0/O requirement.
subjective_observations: IBM Plex Sans has a roomier, calmer texture than the two condensed candidates; its I/1/l forms remain fairly recognizable at 18–32 px.
Noto Sans Display and IBM Plex Sans Condensed save horizontal space, but their O/0 distinction is subtle at 14 px. Source Sans Pro is compact without the same narrow texture.

No default specimen uses a slashed zero. The search rewards compact/tabular metadata but does not score confusion between O and 0. If that requirement is strict, continue with a measured identifier test or inspect a mono alternative rather than accepting the top rank.
briefs.change_from_baseline: The original IBM Plex Sans suggestion becomes a specific verified Regular/Bold pair. Atkinson Hyperlegible cannot be compared because it is absent from this catalog. The harness supplies actual compact alternatives but does not prove superior legibility.
briefs.unfamiliar_option: No clearly unfamiliar family emerged in this shortlist; narrower exact styles were useful.
briefs.remaining_validation: Actual controls, contrast, platform text rasterization, and identifier recognition remain untested.

briefs.decision: Use one family for the next reading-layout prototype: Noto Serif SemiCondensed with its matching italic; keep Untitled Serif as an aesthetic alternative requiring rights review.

Noto Serif Display Condensed has much finer strokes and a taller, tighter texture. I would reject it for this long-reading body role at 16 px despite its equal heuristic score.

briefs.decision: Explore Election Day Expanded for the large title with Inter UI for small mission copy; Martian Mono is the stronger single-family alternative. This is a pairing hypothesis, not a completed product choice.
subjective_observations: Election Day Expanded makes a clear visual departure from the baseline: double-line, squared letterforms create an arcade/sci-fi voice at 32–64 px. At 14 px its outlined mission text looks busy and fragile.
Martian Mono is less theatrical but stays readable in the 14 px mission fixture, and its slashed zero is clearly visible.
ETC Trispace Regular Extended creates a spacious, thin, cinematic title. The same width makes mission copy long and less economical.
Inter UI is much more compact in the mission-text specimen than the three title candidates. Their combination still needs inspection together in a real game layout.
briefs.change_from_baseline: Orbitron and Rajdhani are absent. The harness exposed Election Day Expanded, Martian Mono, and ETC Trispace with exact source files and visibly different behavior.
briefs.unfamiliar_option: Election Day Expanded and ETC Trispace were useful discoveries absent from the unaided baseline.
briefs.remaining_validation: Election Day Expanded and ETC Trispace have unknown rights status. No game engine, title/mission composition, or production license has been validated.

remaining_limits: Subjective visual judgments by one agent, with no blinded comparison, randomization, human subjects, or statistical inference.
The baseline was named recommendations, not a rendered control condition. Only two briefs had eligible baseline files in this catalog.
The index was already built; setup, fetch, rebuild, Windows/Linux, MCP transport, and end application deployment were not tested by this evaluator.

The search does not interpret warmth, restraint, literary tone, or sci-fi semantics beyond documented aliases and literal name matches. Adding warm restrained literary left the game shortlist unchanged and disclosed all three terms as unmodeled.
Equal heuristic scores are not equal design suitability. Noto Serif Display Condensed ranked alongside body-friendly options but was visually rejected for small reading text.
Specimens use HarfBuzz/FreeType unhinted outlines. Their successful coverage is not proof of browser/game/Word parity.
Unknown rights remain unknown. No font licensing clearance, installation, redistribution, or deployment was performed.
conclusion: The harness materially improves evidence and exposes useful alternative files. It does not establish a universal improvement in taste or readability. Keeping the baseline remained the preferred direction for the museum and provisional dashboard.
